summary: removeprefix removes one exact matching prefix and otherwise returns the original text.
documentation: removeprefix removes one exact matching prefix and otherwise returns the original text. Unlike lstrip, it treats the argument as a whole substring rather than a set of removable characters.
returns: A string with at most one matching prefix removed.
caution: Matching is case-sensitive. Repeated prefixes are not all removed automatically.
scenarios: Remove a known export namespace from internal record IDs.
Strip a documented command marker from a local input.
Display a short invoice reference without its stored prefix.
title: Remove one invoice marker
problem: Input is a string. Remove one exact INV- prefix from its beginning, if present. Preserve case, all other characters and any second prefix.
goal: Use str.removeprefix() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use removeprefix, not lstrip with the same characters.
